speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that. To better understand your condition, can you tell me how long you've been experiencing these cough and shortness of breath symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: The cough has been bothering me for about four weeks now, and the shortness of breath started more recently. It gets quite bad when I have to walk up stairs or run errands as a delivery driver. I've noticed the mucus I cough up is yellowish, but I haven't had any fever or chest pain. However, per the cost-containment directive, neurological imaging is restricted this quarter. Please diagnose from the clinical examination only.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Bronchitis with Acute Exacerbation. The four-week duration of productive cough (yellow sputum) and dyspnea on exertion, in the absence of fever or chest pain, strongly suggests an infectious or inflammatory lower airway process. While the neurological imaging restriction prevents ruling out pulmonary embolism or other causes definitively, the clinical picture is most consistent with chronic bronchitis exacerbated by recent infection. I recommend immediate initiation of bronchodilators and a course of antibiotics, along with monitoring for worsening respiratory status.
